decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn both wrists toward top-down approaches, left toward yellow nut and right toward gray nut. Use gradual increments to preserve elbow-up continuity; final alignment will be checked visually.
Complete vertical wrist orientation and approach yellow and gray nuts from above. RGB calibration suggests table lower than first estimate; descend to about 0.928 m EE and inspect before closing.
Use wrist images to center nuts between fingers, then close both grippers fully and make a short test lift. Retention must be checked from images, not gripper commands.

Both nuts remain between the fingers after lifting. Carry yellow leftward to its yellow bolt and gray rightward to its gray bolt, keeping clearance, then lower to an inspection height above the bolt tops.
Wrist views show bolt tips ahead of the nut holes. Make a small forward alignment correction and lower toward thread engagement, then pause to inspect rather than assume insertion.
Both bolt tips now appear inside the matching nut holes. Begin a slow clockwise threading stroke with a small downward feed, keeping the grippers closed and nut axes upright.

The rotated wrist views reveal lateral offset rather than confirmed engagement. Shift both held nuts toward the bolt axes in negative world Y, then lower slightly and recheck before further tightening.
The bolt shafts are now laterally centered. Lower both nuts gently to engage the tips, then apply a short clockwise turn and inspect alignment and depth.
Yellow nut has tilted against its bolt, so lift it clear for recovery. Gray appears more coaxial; apply a limited clockwise stroke with very small feed while staying within wrist range.

Place the tilted yellow nut in a clear left-side area for a fresh upright grasp. Open the right gripper and reset its yaw for another tightening stroke, checking whether the gray nut stays on its bolt.
Gray nut stayed upright on the bolt after release. Regrasp it and make another clockwise stroke with gentle feed. Lower the left hand toward the now-upright yellow nut for visual centering.
Center and regrasp the upright yellow nut, then test-lift it. Release gray and reset the right wrist without reversing the nut, preparing another clockwise tightening stroke.
Yellow is retained upright; carry it above its bolt with extra clearance and corrected XY. Regrasp gray and apply another limited clockwise stroke with gentle downward feed.
Lower the centered yellow nut toward the bolt tip without turning yet. Release gray and reset the right wrist clockwise-stroke range while leaving the nut on the bolt.

Yellow's tip is still ahead of the hole in this wrist orientation. Make a small planar centering correction before deeper insertion. Continue gray with another regrasp and clockwise tightening stroke.
Yellow's bolt tip now enters the hole; lower gently and start a short clockwise stroke. Release gray and lift the open right hand clear to inspect the assembled pair rather than assume completion.
Gray remains upright and seated after release. Open the left gripper and reset its yaw for repeated clockwise yellow tightening strokes, allowing the nut to settle without reversing it.
Yellow did not stay coaxial after release. Regrasp and lift the tilted nut clear, moving to an open left-side area for an upright reset. Leave the seated gray pair undisturbed.
Set the tilted yellow nut down in the clear area, release, and lift the open fingers slightly so its resting orientation can be checked before another grasp.
The yellow nut has settled with its hole upward. Recenter the left hand over its new location using head and wrist views, descend to grasp height, and close without dragging it.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lift and carry the upright yellow nut above its bolt, leaving the right arm stationary and open.
Correct the small lateral offset seen in the left wrist and lower the upright nut toward the bolt tip. Pause at the approach height to assess insertion before turning.
The yellow nut appears to contact the bolt off-center. Lift to relieve contact, move toward the shaft along the wrist-view vertical axis, and return only to a shallow approach height.
Yellow slipped out and is visibly on the table left of its bolt. Approach its new position with open fingers and regrasp at table height, leaving gray undisturbed.
Lift the centered yellow nut well clear, then position over the bolt axis estimated from its base in the calibrated head image. Maintain upright orientation and closed grasp.
The yellow bolt and nut are centered laterally. Descend vertically without adding XY corrections or twist, stopping at a shallow insertion height to inspect.
Insertion depth remains ambiguous in one wrist view. Lift clear and turn the held yellow nut by a quarter-turn to obtain an orthogonal alignment view before attempting contact again.
The orthogonal view confirms near-coaxial XY. Apply only a 2 mm centering correction and descend more deeply, slowing near contact; keep the yellow nut upright and closed.

Contact has tipped the yellow nut. Relieve contact, shift 12 mm toward the shaft along the newly observed wrist direction, then return only to a shallow contact height. Do not infer fastening from contact.
Release the yellow nut at the corrected contact location and lift the open hand to inspect whether it settles coaxially or falls away. The visible tilt is not evidence of engagement.
Yellow has settled upright around the bolt after release. Descend with open fingers and regrasp the seated nut at its current height, preparing clockwise tightening without disturbing the gray pair.
Apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke to the upright yellow nut with only 2 mm total downward feed. Keep the right hand open and stationary over the gray pair.
Yellow now appears coaxial with its bolt visible in the hole. Release the nut and reset wrist yaw with open fingers for another clockwise tightening stroke; verify it stays seated.
Correct the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Regrasp yellow and execute the planned second clockwise tightening stroke, keeping the right arm stationary.
Release yellow and reset the left wrist with open fingers for a final controlled tightening stroke. The nut remains visibly seated; do not lift it.
Regrasp the seated yellow nut and make one further clockwise stroke with gentle feed, then inspect the exposed bolt depth before releasing and moving to red.
Release the visibly seated yellow pair and lift clear. Move the open left hand toward the remaining red nut without crossing the arms; keep gray undisturbed.
Approach the red nut from above in the left workspace, using the calibrated head view for coarse centering and stopping above grasp height for wrist-image refinement.
Refine the red-nut approach from the wrist image: move slightly forward and left while lowering to grasp height. Keep fingers open for a final centering check.
Center and close on the red nut, lift vertically with clearance, then carry it above the matching red bolt. Verify retention and alignment from the next wrist view.
The transfer suffix was rejected before motion. Replan from the observed lifted pose using smaller 4 mm XY increments to carry the retained red nut above its bolt while preserving joint continuity.
The red nut remains upright and laterally centered over its bolt. Lower vertically to a shallow engagement height and pause to inspect before any tightening.
The red bolt tip is visible inside the nut opening. Lower a few millimeters, then try a slow clockwise engagement stroke with minimal feed and inspect for tilt or lateral displacement.
The red nut appears coaxial after the first turn. Release it and reset wrist yaw with open fingers, leaving its depth unchanged and checking that it remains seated.
Red remains seated after release. Regrasp and make a second clockwise tightening stroke with 3 mm total feed, then inspect the bolt depth.
Release the red nut and reset wrist yaw with open fingers, keeping its seated position undisturbed for the next clockwise stroke.
Regrasp the still-upright red nut and make another clockwise stroke with a small downward feed. Keep the other pair and right arm undisturbed.
Release red and reset the wrist with open fingers for one more controlled clockwise tightening stroke, without raising or reversing the nut.
Make a further clockwise tightening stroke on the seated red nut with minimal downward feed. The gray and yellow pairs remain untouched.
Release red and reset wrist yaw with open fingers. Its bolt remains visible within the nut; prepare one final small-feed tightening stroke before clearing the workspace.
Regrasp red and apply the final planned clockwise stroke with only 2 mm downward feed. Inspect the seated pair before opening and returning both arms.
Open both grippers and lift clear of the seated pairs, then begin resetting wrist yaw in free space. Verify all nuts remain on their matching bolts before returning to origin.
All three pairs remain on the table after release. Retract both open arms within their own workspaces, gradually restoring wrist orientation while preserving the elbow-up configuration.
Complete the gradual return to the observed initial EE positions and orientations with both grippers open. The matching pairs remain visibly seated; monitor for episode termination.
Remove the small final tracking offset at origin, then hold the arms still with open grippers while checking for termination and stability of the assembled pairs.
Hold both open hands at origin without disturbing the three seated pairs; allow settling and monitor the episode status.
The episode remains active and gray's depth is less clear from origin. Reapproach the gray pair with the open right hand for a closer inspection, leaving the left arm and other pairs undisturbed.
Finish the right wrist's vertical orientation and lower the open fingers around the gray nut for a close depth and centering check. Keep the left hand at origin.
Gray is upright and centered but still shows exposed internal threads. Lower to its grasp level, regrasp, and add one controlled clockwise stroke with gentle feed.
Release the gray nut and reset wrist yaw with open fingers, leaving the nut seated and avoiding reverse torque. Check that alignment is maintained before another short stroke.
Regrasp the seated gray nut and make a short clockwise tightening stroke with 3 mm total feed, keeping the other pairs untouched and maintaining wrist-range margin.
Release gray, lift the open right hand clear, and reset its yaw in free space for a gradual return to origin. Correct the left arm's small accumulated origin offset.
Gray remains seated after release. Retract the open right arm toward origin while gradually restoring its initial wrist tilt, preserving elbow-up continuity and leaving all pairs undisturbed.
Complete the right arm's gradual return to its initial EE pose with both grippers open. Keep the three seated pairs undisturbed and check for episode termination.

The episode remains active. Yellow received fewer seated tightening strokes than the other pairs; reapproach it with open fingers for a cautious additional tightening check while the right arm settles at origin.
Complete the vertical approach over yellow and lower open fingers to its seated height. Inspect centering and thread depth before applying any further turn.
Center the left fingers over yellow, regrasp, and add a short clockwise tightening stroke with less than 2 mm feed. Keep red and gray undisturbed.
Finish yellow with a short clockwise stroke and 1 mm feed, release, and lift the open left hand clear to inspect stability. Correct the right hand's small origin offset.
Yellow remains upright and seated after release. Reset the open left wrist in free space and retract slightly, preserving elbow-up continuity before returning to origin.
Retract the open left arm and gradually restore its initial wrist tilt, keeping the elbow-up branch continuous. Maintain the right hand at origin and leave all pairs untouched.
Complete the left arm's gradual return to its initial pose with both grippers open, maintaining configuration continuity and leaving the seated pairs undisturbed.
Correct the small residual at origin, then hold both hands open and stationary while monitoring the stability of the three seated pairs and episode status.
Maintain both arms at origin with open grippers and leave the stable matching pairs undisturbed while monitoring episode status.
The episode remains active and gray still shows exposed threads. Reapproach gray and red with open fingers for additional depth checks, keeping each arm in its own workspace.
Complete vertical approaches around the seated red and gray nuts with open fingers. Stop at their current grasp heights for a close alignment and depth check.
Both nuts are centered and upright. Regrasp red and gray, then add a controlled clockwise stroke with 3 mm total feed, keeping the yellow pair untouched.
Release both seated nuts, lift the open hands clear, and begin resetting yaw in free space. Leave the three matching pairs undisturbed while returning to origin.
